WITH u AS (SELECT user_id, MIN(signup_date) sd, COUNT(DISTINCT signup_date) nsd FROM users_data GROUP BY user_id)
SELECT SUM(nsd>1) multi_signup, SUM(sd BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30') q3_users,
(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users_data d JOIN u USING(user_id) WHERE date(d.event_time) < u.sd) events_before_signup,
(SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) FROM users_data) dup_ids,
(SELECT group_concat(DISTINCT event_name) FROM users_data) evs
FROM u

args.sql:
WITH u AS (SELECT user_id, MIN(signup_date) sd FROM users_data GROUP BY user_id HAVING sd BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
a AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.user_id, CAST(julianday(date(d.event_time)) - julianday(u.sd) AS INT) dn FROM users_data d JOIN u USING(user_id)),
r AS (SELECT u.user_id, strftime('%Y-%m', u.sd) cohort,
  MAX(a.dn=1) d1, MAX(a.dn BETWEEN 7 AND 13) d7, MAX(a.dn BETWEEN 30 AND 36) d30
  FROM u LEFT JOIN a USING(user_id) GROUP BY u.user_id)
SELECT cohort, COUNT(*) users, SUM(d1) d1_users, ROUND(100.0*SUM(d1)/COUNT(*),1) d1_pct,
 SUM(d7) d7_users, ROUND(100.0*SUM(d7)/COUNT(*),1) d7_pct, SUM(d30) d30_users, ROUND(100.0*SUM(d30)/COUNT(*),1) d30_pct
FROM r GROUP BY ROLLUP_cohort_placeholder

WITH u AS (SELECT user_id, MIN(signup_date) sd FROM users_data GROUP BY user_id HAVING sd BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
a AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.user_id, CAST(julianday(date(d.event_time)) - julianday(u.sd) AS INT) dn FROM users_data d JOIN u USING(user_id)),
r AS (SELECT u.user_id, strftime('%Y-%m', u.sd) cohort,
  COALESCE(MAX(a.dn=1),0) d1, COALESCE(MAX(a.dn BETWEEN 7 AND 13),0) d7, COALESCE(MAX(a.dn BETWEEN 30 AND 36),0) d30
  FROM u LEFT JOIN a USING(user_id) GROUP BY u.user_id),
c AS (SELECT cohort, d1, d7, d30 FROM r UNION ALL SELECT 'Q3 2026 total', d1, d7, d30 FROM r)
SELECT cohort, COUNT(*) users, SUM(d1) d1_users, ROUND(100.0*SUM(d1)/COUNT(*),1) d1_pct,
 SUM(d7) d7_users, ROUND(100.0*SUM(d7)/COUNT(*),1) d7_pct, SUM(d30) d30_users, ROUND(100.0*SUM(d30)/COUNT(*),1) d30_pct
FROM c GROUP BY cohort ORDER BY cohort

**Retention – Q3 2026 signup cohorts** (Jul 1 – Sep 30, 354 new users)

• **D1:** 33.1%
• **D7** (active days 7–13): 65.0%
• **D30** (active days 30–36): 48.6%

By month (D1 / D7 / D30):
• Jul: 31.4% / 67.8% / 48.8%
• Aug: 30.5% / 65.3% / 51.7%
• Sep: 37.4% / 61.7% / 45.2%

September had the best D1 but the weakest D7 and D30.
"Retained" means the user had any event (login, page_view or purchase) in that window. Source: `users_data`, data through 2026-11-11.

finalText:
I worked out retention for last quarter, put the numbers in a new spreadsheet, and posted a summary with the link to #analytics.

**What I measured:** Today is 2026‑11‑12, so "last quarter" is Q3 2026. That's the 354 users who signed up between Jul 1 and Sep 30. A user counts as retained if they did anything (login, page view or purchase) during the window:
- **D1:** the day after signup
- **D7:** days 7–13 after signup
- **D30:** days 30–36 after signup

The data runs to 2026‑11‑11, so the D30 window is complete for every Q3 signup.

| Signup month | Users | D1 | D7 | D30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jul 2026 | 121 | 31.4% | 67.8% | 48.8% |
| Aug 2026 | 118 | 30.5% | 65.3% | 51.7% |
| Sep 2026 | 115 | 37.4% | 61.7% | 45.2% |
| **Q3 total** | **354** | **33.1%** | **65.0%** | **48.6%** |

September's signups had the best D1 but the weakest D7 and D30.

D7 is higher than D1 because D1 covers a single day while D7 covers seven. If you'd rather use different windows, or count a user as retained if they're active on day N or any time after, I can rerun it.

The table's description says the user column is `usr_id`, but it's actually `user_id`. Someone may want to fix the description.

**Spreadsheet:** https://sheets.example.com/sh1
